claims.claim: In May 1967 Peter Houldcroft at TWI used a 300 W CO2 laser with coaxial oxygen assist to cut 1 mm steel sheet.
claims.episode_span: In May 1967 at the Welding Institute near Cambridge, Peter Houldcroft directed a focused beam from a 300-watt carbon-dioxide laser across a sheet of steel while a coaxial jet of oxygen flowed through the same nozzle.
claims.supporting_quote: conducted in May 1967 when Peter Houldcroft used an oxygen assist gas to cut 1mm thick steel sheet with a focused CO 2 laser beam

claims.claim: The same apparatus achieved cuts up to 2.5 mm thick at speeds up to 1 m/min.
claims.episode_span: Within months the same 300-watt machine was reported to cut steel up to 2.5 millimeters thick at speeds approaching one meter per minute.
claims.supporting_quote: Cuts were made using oxygen assist gas in high carbon tool steel and stainless steel up to 2.5mm thick at speeds up to 1m/min.
